claim: The ventricular-subventricular zone (V-SVZ) on the walls of the lateral ventricles harbors the largest neurogenic niche in the adult mouse brain.
source: The ventricular-subventricular zone (V-SVZ), on the walls of the lateral ventricles, harbors the largest neurogenic niche in the adult mouse brain.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that is supported by established scientific knowledge about adult neurogenesis in mice.

claim: Neural stem/progenitor cells (NSPCs) in different locations within the V-SVZ produce different subtypes of new neurons for the olfactory bulb.
source: Previous work has shown that neural stem/progenitor cells (NSPCs) in different locations within the V-SVZ produce different subtypes of new neurons for the olfactory bulb.
evidence: This claim references previous work, indicating it is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Two populations of NSPCs reside in largely non-overlapping domains in either the dorsal or ventral V-SVZ.
source: Here, we present a single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset of the adult mouse V-SVZ revealing two populations of NSPCs that reside in largely non-overlapping domains in either the dorsal or ventral V-SVZ.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Regional differences in gene expression were validated using a single-nucleus RNA-sequencing reference dataset of regionally microdissected domains of the V-SVZ.
source: These regional differences in gene expression were further validated using a single-nucleus RNA-sequencing reference dataset of regionally microdissected domains of the V-SVZ and by immunocytochemistry and RNAscope localization.
evidence: This describes the validation methods used in the study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: Two subpopulations of young neurons have gene expression profiles consistent with a dorsal or ventral origin.
source: We also identify two subpopulations of young neurons that have gene expression profiles consistent with a dorsal or ventral origin.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of the single-cell RNA-sequencing data.

claim: A subset of genes are dynamically expressed but maintained in the ventral or dorsal lineages.
source: Interestingly, a subset of genes are dynamically expressed, but maintained, in the ventral or dorsal lineages.
evidence: This observation is derived from the analysis of gene expression patterns across the neurogenic lineage.

claim: B cells in the V-SVZ are a subpopulation of astrocytes that function as neural stem/progenitor cells.
source: This neurogenic niche includes the ventricular-subventricular zones in the walls of the lateral ventricles (V-SVZ), home to a subpopulation of astrocytes (B cells) that function as the NSPCs (Chaker et al., 2016; Doetsch et al., 1997; Ihrie and Alvarez-Buylla, 2011; Lim and Alvarez-Buylla, 2014; Mirzadeh et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: B cells generate intermediate progenitors (C cells) that give rise to neuroblasts (A cells) that migrate to the olfactory bulb.
source: B cells generate intermediate progenitors (C cells) that, in turn, give rise to neuroblasts (A cells) that migrate to the olfactory bulb (OB) (Obernier et al., 2018; Ponti et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the established lineage progression in the V-SVZ, supported by citations.

claim: A subpopulation of B cells generate oligodendrocytes.
source: A subpopulation of B cells also generate oligodendrocytes (Figueres-Oñate et al., 2019; Gonzalez-Perez, 2014; Kazanis et al., 2017; Menn et al., 2006; Nait-Oumesmar et al., 1999; Picard-Riera et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Adult NSPCs are heterogeneous and specialized depending on their location for the generation of specific types of neurons and possibly glia.
source: From the initial interpretation that adult NSPCs are multipotent and able to generate a wide range of neural cell types (Morshead et al., 1994; Reynolds and Weiss, 1992; van der Kooy and Weiss, 2000), more recent work suggests that the adult NSPCs are heterogeneous and specialized, depending on their location, for the generation of specific types of neurons, and possibly glia (Chaker et al., 2016; Delgado et al., 2020; Fiorelli et al., 2015; Merkle et al., 2014, Merkle et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim contrasts earlier interpretations with more recent findings, supported by citations.

claim: Previous single-cell sequencing experiments in the V-SVZ have described the many broad classes of cells that reside in the niche.
source: Previous single-cell sequencing experiments in the V-SVZ have described the many broad classes of cells that reside in the niche.
evidence: This is a summary statement about prior research in the field.

claim: Transcriptional analyses after cell sorting have identified stages in the B-C-A cell lineage.
source: For example, transcriptional analyses after cell sorting have identified stages in the B-C-A cell lineage (Borrett et al., 2020; Codega et al., 2014; Dulken et al., 2017; Xie et al., 2020), as well as populations of NSPCs that appear to activate after injury (Llorens-Bobadilla et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous transcriptional studies.

claim: Profiling of the entire niche has highlighted differences between quiescent and activated B cells.
source: Profiling of the entire niche has highlighted differences between quiescent and activated B cells (Mizrak et al., 2020; Zywitza et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous profiling studies.

claim: The differences among B cells of equivalent activation state or the B cell heterogeneity that leads to the generation of diverse neuronal subtypes remain poorly understood.
source: However, the differences among B cells of equivalent activation state (e.g. quiescent, primed, or activated) or the B cell heterogeneity that leads to the generation of diverse neuronal subtypes remain poorly understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge, setting up the rationale for the study.

claim: NSPC heterogeneity is largely driven by their location within the adult V-SVZ.
source: NSPC heterogeneity, interestingly, is largely driven by their location within the adult V-SVZ.
evidence: This is a key concept supported by the literature and the findings of this study.

claim: Young neurons in the OB originate over a wide territory in the walls of the lateral ventricles.
source: This concept explains why young neurons in the OB originate over such a wide territory in the walls of the lateral ventricles.
evidence: This is an inference based on the regional heterogeneity of NSPCs.

claim: Multiple studies have begun to identify regional differences in gene expression among the lateral, septal, and subcallosal walls of the lateral ventricles.
source: Multiple studies have begun to identify regional differences in gene expression among the lateral, septal, and subcallosal walls of the lateral ventricles (Delgado et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Differences in gene expression of B cells from the septal and lateral walls of the lateral ventricles have been recently observed.
source: For example, differences in gene expression of B cells from the septal and lateral walls of the lateral ventricles have been recently observed (Mizrak et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Pax6 and Hopx-expressing cells correspond to dorsal V-SVZ progenitors.
source: Other studies have shown that Pax6 and Hopx-expressing cells correspond to dorsal V-SVZ progenitors (Hack et al., 2005; Kohwi et al., 2005; Zweifel et al., 2018), and Vax1-expressing young neuroblasts are derived from ventral progenitors (Coré et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Vax1-expressing young neuroblasts are derived from ventral progenitors.
source: Other studies have shown that Pax6 and Hopx-expressing cells correspond to dorsal V-SVZ progenitors (Hack et al., 2005; Kohwi et al., 2005; Zweifel et al., 2018), and Vax1-expressing young neuroblasts are derived from ventral progenitors (Coré et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Spatially defined lineage-tracing studies using microinjections of viruses have identified subdomains of the V-SVZ that give rise to specific subtypes of OB neurons.
source: Spatially defined lineage-tracing studies using microinjections of viruses have identified subdomains of the V-SVZ that give rise to specific subtypes of OB neurons (Merkle et al., 2014; Merkle et al., 2007; Ventura and Goldman, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to lineage-tracing studies.

claim: Regional subdomains largely follow the territories defined by developmentally regulated transcription factors including Pax6, Nkx2.1, Nkx6.2, and Emx1.
source: Lineage-tracing studies have demonstrated that these regional subdomains largely follow the territories defined by developmentally regulated transcription factors including Pax6, Nkx2.1, Nkx6.2, and Emx1 (Delgado et al., 2020; Delgado and Lim, 2015; Kohwi et al., 2007, Kohwi et al., 2005; Merkle et al., 2014; Willaime-Morawek et al., 2006; Young et al., 2007), but the molecular differences among B cells underlying their regionally-restricted potential are largely unknown.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to lineage-tracing studies.

claim: The molecular differences among B cells underlying their regionally-restricted potential are largely unknown.
source: Lineage-tracing studies have demonstrated that these regional subdomains largely follow the territories defined by developmentally regulated transcription factors including Pax6, Nkx2.1, Nkx6.2, and Emx1 (Delgado et al., 2020; Delgado and Lim, 2015; Kohwi et al., 2007, Kohwi et al., 2005; Merkle et al., 2014; Willaime-Morawek et al., 2006; Young et al., 2007), but the molecular differences among B cells underlying their regionally-restricted potential are largely unknown.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: Clustering analysis reveals strong dorso-ventral differences in lateral wall B cells.
source: Clustering analysis reveals strong dorso-ventral differences in lateral wall B cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the clustering analysis of the single-cell RNA-sequencing data.

claim: Validation of differential gene expression patterns has revealed the anatomical boundary that separates dorsal and ventral B cell domains.
source: Validation of these differential gene expression patterns has revealed the anatomical boundary that separates these dorsal and ventral B cell domains.
evidence: This is a finding from the validation experiments using immunocytochemistry and RNAscope.

claim: The analysis identifies subpopulations of A cells defined by maturation state and dorso-ventral origin.
source: Additionally, our analysis identifies subpopulations of A cells defined by maturation state and dorso-ventral origin.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of A cell clusters in the single-cell RNA-sequencing data.

claim: A subset of dorso-ventral B cell transcriptional differences are retained through the C and A cell stages of the lineage.
source: We also find that a subset of dorso-ventral B cell transcriptional differences are retained through the C and A cell stages of the lineage.
evidence: This is a finding from the lineage analysis of gene expression patterns.

claim: The lateral wall of the lateral ventricle was dissected from hGFAP:GFP mice at postnatal day (P) 29–35 (n=8).
source: For whole single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq), we dissected the lateral wall of the lateral ventricle from hGFAP:GFP mice at postnatal day (P) 29–35 (n=8, Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure for sample collection.

claim: Two male and two female samples were dissociated and multiplexed by labeling cells with sample-specific MULTI-seq barcodes.
source: To determine possible sex differences in downstream analyses, two male and two female samples (n=four samples total) were dissociated and multiplexed by labeling cells with sample-specific MULTI-seq barcodes (McGinnis et al., 2019a).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure for sample multiplexing.

claim: Cells carrying multiple barcodes or a high number of mRNA reads (4128 out of 35,025 cells, 11.7%) were considered doublets and were eliminated from downstream analysis.
source: Cells carrying multiple barcodes or a high number of mRNA reads (4128 out of 35,025 cells, 11.7%) were considered doublets and were eliminated from downstream analysis.
evidence: This describes the quality control procedure for the single-cell RNA-sequencing data.

claim: The clustering of lateral wall V-SVZ cells was not driven by sample, technical replicate, or sex.
source: The clustering of lateral wall V-SVZ cells was not driven by sample, technical replicate, or sex (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–J).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of potential batch effects in the data.

claim: 37 clusters were identified, with 14 clusters corresponding to cell types within the neurogenic lineage: NSPCs (B cells), intermediate progenitors (C cells), and neuroblasts (A cells).
source: We identified 37 clusters, with 14 clusters corresponding to cell types within the neurogenic lineage: NSPCs (B cells), intermediate progenitors (C cells), and neuroblasts (A cells) (Doetsch et al., 1999; Obernier et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the results of the clustering analysis.

claim: Cell clusters corresponding to parenchymal astrocytes, ependymal cells, neurons, oligodendroglia, microglia, pericytes, vascular smooth muscle cells, and endothelial cells were identified.
source: In addition, our analysis identified cell clusters corresponding to parenchymal astrocytes, ependymal cells, neurons, oligodendroglia, microglia, pericytes, vascular smooth muscle cells, and endothelial cells (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This describes the results of the clustering analysis.

claim: 51.85% of B cells expressed Gfap.
source: A fraction of both populations expressed Gfap: 51.85% of B cells (clusters 5, 13, 14, and 22) and 24.37% of parenchymal astrocytes (clusters 21, 26, and 29).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: 24.37% of parenchymal astrocytes expressed Gfap.
source: A fraction of both populations expressed Gfap: 51.85% of B cells (clusters 5, 13, 14, and 22) and 24.37% of parenchymal astrocytes (clusters 21, 26, and 29).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: Among all cells captured in the scRNAseq analysis, only B cells, parenchymal astrocytes or ependymal cells expressed high levels of Gfap.
source: Note that across all cells captured in our scRNAseq analysis, only B cells, parenchymal astrocytes or ependymal cells expressed high levels of Gfap.
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: Among B cells, parenchymal astrocytes, and ependymal cells, B cells had the highest average expression of Gfap (4.41 for B cells, 1.00 for astrocytes, 0.298 for ependymal cells, values in SCT corrected counts).
source: Furthermore, among these three cell types, B cells had the highest average expression of Gfap (4.41 for B cells, 1.00 for astrocytes, 0.298 for ependymal cells, values in SCT corrected counts).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: 88.9% of B cells expressed S100a6.
source: Other markers, like S100a6 (Kjell et al., 2020) (88.9% of B cells; 54% of parenchymal astrocytes, and 80% of ependymal cells) and Thbs4 (Zywitza et al., 2018) (45% of B cells; 28.77% in parenchymal astrocytes, 2.88% in ependymal cells) are also expressed preferentially in B cells, but they alone do not distinguish these two cell populations (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: 54% of parenchymal astrocytes expressed S100a6.
source: Other markers, like S100a6 (Kjell et al., 2020) (88.9% of B cells; 54% of parenchymal astrocytes, and 80% of ependymal cells) and Thbs4 (Zywitza et al., 2018) (45% of B cells; 28.77% in parenchymal astrocytes, 2.88% in ependymal cells) are also expressed preferentially in B cells, but they alone do not distinguish these two cell populations (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: 80% of ependymal cells expressed S100a6.
source: Other markers, like S100a6 (Kjell et al., 2020) (88.9% of B cells; 54% of parenchymal astrocytes, and 80% of ependymal cells) and Thbs4 (Zywitza et al., 2018) (45% of B cells; 28.77% in parenchymal astrocytes, 2.88% in ependymal cells) are also expressed preferentially in B cells, but they alone do not distinguish these two cell populations (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: 45% of B cells expressed Thbs4.
source: Other markers, like S100a6 (Kjell et al., 2020) (88.9% of B cells; 54% of parenchymal astrocytes, and 80% of ependymal cells) and Thbs4 (Zywitza et al., 2018) (45% of B cells; 28.77% in parenchymal astrocytes, 2.88% in ependymal cells) are also expressed preferentially in B cells, but they alone do not distinguish these two cell populations (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: 28.77% of parenchymal astrocytes expressed Thbs4.
source: Other markers, like S100a6 (Kjell et al., 2020) (88.9% of B cells; 54% of parenchymal astrocytes, and 80% of ependymal cells) and Thbs4 (Zywitza et al., 2018) (45% of B cells; 28.77% in parenchymal astrocytes, 2.88% in ependymal cells) are also expressed preferentially in B cells, but they alone do not distinguish these two cell populations (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: 2.88% of ependymal cells expressed Thbs4.
source: Other markers, like S100a6 (Kjell et al., 2020) (88.9% of B cells; 54% of parenchymal astrocytes, and 80% of ependymal cells) and Thbs4 (Zywitza et al., 2018) (45% of B cells; 28.77% in parenchymal astrocytes, 2.88% in ependymal cells) are also expressed preferentially in B cells, but they alone do not distinguish these two cell populations (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: B cells had a higher expression of Maff, Zfp36, Bex4, Lgals3, and Anxa2 compared to parenchymal astrocytes.
source: We found that B cells had a higher expression of Maff, Zfp36, Bex4, Lgals3, and Anxa2 compared to parenchymal astrocytes, which in turn were enriched for Clmn, Atp13a4, Eps8, Pcdh7, and Syne1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Parenchymal astrocytes were enriched for Clmn, Atp13a4, Eps8, Pcdh7, and Syne1 compared to B cells.
source: We found that B cells had a higher expression of Maff, Zfp36, Bex4, Lgals3, and Anxa2 compared to parenchymal astrocytes, which in turn were enriched for Clmn, Atp13a4, Eps8, Pcdh7, and Syne1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Genes associated with synapse regulation, macroautophagy, and dendrite development and morphogenesis were overrepresented in parenchymal astrocytes compared to B cells.
source: Genes associated with synapse regulation (GO:0051965 and 0051963), macroautophagy (GO: 0016241), and dendrite development and morphogenesis (GO: 0016358 and 0048813), among others, were overrepresented in parenchymal astrocytes compared to B cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: B cells were enriched in terms associated with RNA regulation and mitochondrial regulation.
source: In contrast, B cells were enriched in terms associated with RNA regulation (GO:0000463, 0034471, 0000956, and 0000966) and mitochondrial regulation (GO:006626, 0073655, 0090201, and 0010823) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: The majority of cells in the scRNA-Seq dataset were part of the neurogenic lineage, which is composed of primary progenitors, intermediate progenitors, and young neurons (the B-C-A cell lineage).
source: In our scRNA-Seq dataset, we found that the majority of cells were part of the neurogenic lineage, which is composed of primary progenitors, intermediate progenitors, and young neurons (the B-C-A cell lineage).
evidence: This describes the composition of the dataset.

claim: All B cell clusters expressed Gfap, GFP, and S100a6.
source: As expected, all B cell clusters expressed Gfap, GFP, and S100a6 (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: Quiescent B cells (clusters 5, 14, and 22) are characterized by high expression of Thbs4 and Gfap, no Egfr, and low Ascl1 expression.
source: We identified a subpopulation of B cells as the quiescent B cells (Codega et al., 2014; Llorens-Bobadilla et al., 2015) (clusters 5, 14, and 22) characterized by high expression of Thbs4 and Gfap, no Egfr, and low Ascl1 expression (Figure 2B,E,F,G).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis and clustering.

claim: Cluster 13 corresponds to activated B cells with lower expression of Gfap, GFP, and S100a6, but high Egfr and Ascl1 expression.
source: In contrast, cluster 13 (the neck region of the 'hummingbird') corresponded to activated B cells with lower expression of Gfap, GFP, and S100a6, but high Egfr and Ascl1 expression (Codega et al., 2014; Figure 2B–D,F–G).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis and clustering.

claim: Cluster 13 cells expressed Notum, a marker recently associated with activating qNSPCs.
source: Cluster 13 cells also expressed Notum, a marker recently associated with activating qNSPCs (Mizrak et al., 2020; Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: Cluster 12 was identified as the C cell cluster, which had low expression of astrocytic markers Gfap and GFP, but high expression of Egfr and Ascl1.
source: Bordering cluster 13 in the chest region of the 'bird' was cluster 12, identified as the C cell cluster, which had low expression of astrocytic markers Gfap and GFP (Figure 2B–C), but high expression of Egfr and Ascl1 (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis and clustering.

claim: A high number of cells in cluster 12 were in the S phase (691/992, 69.6%), consistent with cluster 12 corresponding to intermediate progenitors (C cells).
source: We used cell-cycle scoring to classify cells by their G2M, S, or G1 phase (Tirosh et al., 2016) and found that a high number of cells in cluster 12 were in the S phase (691/992, 69.6%, Supplementary file 2), consistent with cluster 12 corresponding to intermediate progenitors (C cells) (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell cycle analysis.

claim: Clusters 10, 16, 17, and 8 correspond to dividing B, C, and A cells, respectively.
source: A closer look at these clusters of mitotic cells in G2 or metaphase (G2M; clusters 10, 16, 17, and 8) showed that their gene expression pattern overlaps with that of the non-dividing neurogenic lineage cell progression: Cluster 10 expresses markers of B cells (GFP, Notum), cluster 16 had markers of C cells (Ascl1), and cluster 8 expresses markers of A cells (Dcx) (Figure 2B–K). This suggests that these clusters correspond to dividing B, C, and A cells, respectively, which have all been previously observed by electron and confocal microscopy in vivo (Doetsch et al., 1997).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression patterns and supported by citations to previous microscopy studies.

claim: The largest number of cells within the neurogenic lineage corresponded to neuroblasts and young neurons (A cells) (clusters 0, 1, 4, 6, and 15).
source: Identified by Dcx expression, the largest number of cells within the neurogenic lineage corresponded to neuroblasts and young neurons (A cells) (clusters 0, 1, 4, 6, and 15; the tail region of the hummingbird) (Figure 2A,J).
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering analysis.

claim: Unbiased clustering subdivided A cells into five subclusters with different gene expression profiles.
source: Interestingly, unbiased clustering subdivided A cells into five subclusters with different gene expression profiles.
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering analysis.

claim: Clusters 6 and 15 contain Dcx+ A cells with proliferative markers (e.g. Mki67).
source: Consistent with previous work showing that a subpopulation of newly generated neurons continues to divide (Lois and Alvarez-Buylla, 1993; Menezes et al., 1995), clusters 6 and 15 contain Dcx+ A cells with proliferative markers (e.g. Mki67) (Figure 2I–K).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: RNA-velocity lineage trajectory reconstruction supports the overall progression from B-C-A cells.
source: The overall progression from B-C-A cells described above is supported by RNA-velocity lineage trajectory reconstruction (La Manno et al., 2018), in which genes defining B, C, and A cells are expressed sequentially in distinct phases in pseudotime (Figure 2L–M).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNA velocity analysis.

claim: Quiescent B cells were subdivided into three clusters: B cell cluster 5 (B(5)), B(14), and B(22).
source: In our scRNA-Seq dataset, we found that quiescent B cells (the head of the 'bird'; Figure 2A) were subdivided into three clusters: B cell cluster 5 (B(5)), B(14), and B(22) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering analysis.

claim: Nkx6.2, a transcription factor expressed in the ventral embryonic and postnatal ventricular zone, is enriched in cluster B(14).
source: For example, Nkx6.2, a transcription factor expressed in the ventral embryonic and postnatal ventricular zone (Merkle et al., 2014; Moreno-Bravo et al., 2010), is enriched in cluster B(14), as are Notum and Lmo1 (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C; Borrett et al., 2020; Mizrak et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis, supported by citations.

claim: Gsx2, a marker of dorsal B cells, is a marker of cluster B(5).
source: Similarly, Gsx2, a marker of dorsal B cells, is a marker of cluster B(5) (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Emx1 is significantly upregulated in cluster B(22).
source: Another known dorsal marker, Emx1, is significantly upregulated in cluster B(22) (Figure 3C, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Cluster B(14) scored more highly for ventral identity on average, while clusters B(5) and B(22) scored more highly for dorsal identity.
source: We found that cluster B(14) scored more highly for ventral identity on average, while clusters B(5) and B(22) scored more highly for dorsal identity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the label transfer analysis.

claim: Urah and Dio2 were highly expressed among GFAP+ cells in the V-SVZ dorsal 'wedge', while lower expression was observed in the intermediate and ventral regions.
source: We found that Urah and Dio2 were highly expressed among GFAP+ cells in the V-SVZ dorsal 'wedge' (the dorso-lateral corner of the V-SVZ enriched in B, C, and A cells), while lower expression was observed in the intermediate and ventral regions (Figure 3J–S).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAscope validation experiments.

claim: Hopx was expressed in B cells in the dorsal wedge with no expression in the intermediate and ventral V-SVZ regions.
source: Hopx was expressed in B cells in the dorsal wedge with no expression in the intermediate and ventral V-SVZ regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1M–Q).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAscope validation experiments.

claim: Cluster B(14) marker Crym was expressed in intermediate and ventral V-SVZ GFAP+ cells, with very little expression in dorsal V-SVZ and wedge regions.
source: Cluster B(14) marker Crym was expressed in intermediate and ventral V-SVZ GFAP+ cells (Figure 3T–X), with very little expression in dorsal V-SVZ and wedge regions (Figure 3T–X).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAscope validation experiments.

claim: Ventral SVZ GFP+ B cells were CRYM+, while dorsal wedge GFP+ cells were negative.
source: Consistent with the RNAscope analysis, ventral SVZ GFP+ B cells were CRYM+, while dorsal wedge GFP+ cells were negative (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunostaining validation experiments.

claim: Only 2.47% GFP+ cells were CRYM+ in the dorsal domain, while 97.67% of the ventral GFP+ B cells were CRYM+.
source: There was a sharp difference with only 2.47% GFP+ cells being CRYM+ in the dorsal domain, while 97.67% of the ventral GFP+ B cells were CRYM+.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the immunostaining validation experiments.

claim: 95.11% ± 2.65 (SD) of the GFP+ B1 cells were CRYM+ in the ventral domain of the V-SVZ.
source: Quantifications in these whole mounts showed that 95.11% ± 2.65 (SD) of the GFP+ B1 cells were CRYM+ in the ventral domain of the V-SVZ.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the whole mount immunostaining experiments.

claim: Only 4.71% ± 1.38 (SD) of the GFP+ B1 cells in the dorsal region were CRYM+ (n=3; T-test, p<0.0001).
source: In contrast, only 4.71% ± 1.38 (SD) of the GFP+ B1 cells in the dorsal region were CRYM+ (n=3; T-test, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the whole mount immunostaining experiments with statistical analysis.

claim: Immunogold staining showed that B1 cells in the ventral domain express CRYM.
source: Immunogold staining showed that B1 cells in the ventral domain express CRYM (Figure 4. J-K).
evidence: This is a finding from the transmission electron microscopy experiments.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in ventral B cells had an overrepresentation of genes involved in the response to growth hormone and retinal ganglion cell axon guidance.
source: We then conducted GO analysis on differentially expressed genes between dorsal B(5+22) and ventral B(14) cells and found that differentially expressed genes in ventral B cells had an overrepresentation of genes involved in the response to growth hormone (GO:0060416) and retinal ganglion cell axon guidance (GO:0031290), while dorsal B cells were associated with oligodendrocyte differentiation (GO:0048709), forebrain generation of neurons (GO:0021872), and central nervous system neuron axonogenesis (GO:0021955)(Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Dorsal B cells were associated with oligodendrocyte differentiation, forebrain generation of neurons, and central nervous system neuron axonogenesis.
source: We then conducted GO analysis on differentially expressed genes between dorsal B(5+22) and ventral B(14) cells and found that differentially expressed genes in ventral B cells had an overrepresentation of genes involved in the response to growth hormone (GO:0060416) and retinal ganglion cell axon guidance (GO:0031290), while dorsal B cells were associated with oligodendrocyte differentiation (GO:0048709), forebrain generation of neurons (GO:0021872), and central nervous system neuron axonogenesis (GO:0021955)(Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: The dorsal network was much more highly interconnected than the ventral network (dorsal clustering coefficient = 0.121, ventral clustering coefficient = 0.005).
source: The dorsal network was much more highly interconnected than the ventral network (dorsal clustering coefficient = 0.121, ventral clustering coefficient = 0.005).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the gene regulatory network analysis.

claim: The central dorsal network was enriched for genes associated with regulation of apoptosis and central nervous system axonogenesis.
source: The central dorsal network was enriched for genes associated with regulation of apoptosis (GO:0042981) and central nervous system axonogenesis (GO:0021955), while ventral networks were enriched for genes associated with cell fate commitment (GO:0045165), regulation of GABAergic synaptic transmission (GO:0032228), and regulation of transcription (GO:0045449).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene regulatory network and gene ontology analysis.

claim: Ventral networks were enriched for genes associated with cell fate commitment, regulation of GABAergic synaptic transmission, and regulation of transcription.
source: The central dorsal network was enriched for genes associated with regulation of apoptosis (GO:0042981) and central nervous system axonogenesis (GO:0021955), while ventral networks were enriched for genes associated with cell fate commitment (GO:0045165), regulation of GABAergic synaptic transmission (GO:0032228), and regulation of transcription (GO:0045449).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene regulatory network and gene ontology analysis.

claim: The dorsal network contained all three genes that make up nuclear receptor subfamily 4A (Nr4a1, Nr4a2, and Nr4a3).
source: Notably, the dorsal network contained all three genes that make up nuclear receptor subfamily 4A (Nr4a1, Nr4a2, and Nr4a3), members of the steroid-thyroid hormone receptor superfamily that are linked to neuronal specification, axon guidance, and neurotransmission (Jeanneteau et al., 2018; Luo et al., 2008; Soldati et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene regulatory network analysis, with supporting citations.

claim: A cells were separated into two main sets of transcriptionally-related clusters: clusters A(15) and A(6) corresponded to A cells with a strong expression of genes associated with mitosis and cell cycle regulation.
source: We found that A cells (Figure 5A) were separated into two main sets of transcriptionally-related clusters: clusters A(15) and A(6) corresponded to A cells with a strong expression of genes associated with mitosis and cell cycle regulation (such as Pclaf, Hmgb2, Rrm2, Mki67, Top2a, and the Mcm gene family) (Figure 5B, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering and gene expression analysis.

claim: Clusters A(1), A(0), and A(4) corresponded to a second set of A cells expressing high levels of genes involved in cell migration, such as Dab1 and Slit2.
source: Clusters A(1), A(0), and A(4) corresponded to a second set of A cells expressing high levels of genes involved in cell migration, such as Dab1 and Slit2 (Figure 5B; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the clustering and gene expression analysis.

claim: Neuron migration and spontaneous synaptic transmission categories were more strongly present in clusters A(0), A(1), and A(4), indicating that these clusters likely correspond to migrating young neurons.
source: We found that neuron migration (GO:0001764) and spontaneous synaptic transmission (GO: 0098814) categories were more strongly present in clusters A(0), A(1), and A(4) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), indicating that these clusters likely correspond to migrating young neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: A cells are organized in a continuum of maturation in UMAP space, with dividing neuroblasts at the top of the A cell cluster group and migrating young neurons at the bottom.
source: This analysis of the GO terms enriched in A cells is consistent with the pseudotime analysis (Figure 2L–M), indicating that A cells are organized in a continuum of maturation in UMAP space, with dividing neuroblasts at the top of the A cell cluster group and migrating young neurons at the bottom.
evidence: This is an inference based on the integration of gene ontology and pseudotime analyses.

claim: The combined expression of genes in dorsoventral axonal guidance and cerebral cortex regionalization was high in clusters A(1) and A(0).
source: Interestingly, the combined expression of genes in dorsoventral axonal guidance (GO:0033563) and cerebral cortex regionalization (GO:0021796), terms associated with the regional specification of the brain, was high in clusters A(1) and A(0), despite individual GO terms not being statistically enriched in these clusters (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: Runx1t1 and Nxph1 were among the most differentially expressed genes in cluster A(1).
source: Additionally, Runx1t1, a transcription factor expressed in young neurons from the medial ganglionic eminence (Chen et al., 2017), and Nxph1, expressed in young migrating neurons from subpallial germinal zones (Batista-Brito et al., 2008), were among the most differentially expressed genes in cluster A(1) (Figure 5B–C, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis, with supporting citations.

claim: Pax6 was the most differentially expressed gene for cluster A(0).
source: Conversely, Pax6, a transcription factor that is highly expressed in the pallium and in the dorsal lateral ganglionic eminence (Ypsilanti and Rubenstein, 2016), was the most differentially expressed gene for cluster A(0) (Figure 5B–C, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis, with a supporting citation.

claim: Vax1 and Pax6 were highly expressed in clusters A(1) and A(0), respectively.
source: Importantly, Vax1 and Pax6, which have been previously found to be differentially expressed by ventrally- and dorsally-born A cells (Coré et al., 2020), were highly expressed in clusters A(1) and A(0), respectively (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis, with a supporting citation.

claim: Gene expression suggests that A cells in cluster A(1) originate from ventral progenitors and A cells in cluster A(0) originate from dorsal progenitors.
source: Taken together, gene expression suggests that A cells in cluster A(1) originate from ventral progenitors and A cells in cluster A(0) originate from dorsal progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression patterns.

claim: Cluster A(1) had cells with high correspondence to A cells found in both the ventral and dorsal dissections (925 predicted dorsal dissection; 761 predicted ventral dissection).
source: In contrast, cluster A(1) had cells with high correspondence to A cells found in both the ventral and dorsal dissections (925 predicted dorsal dissection; 761 predicted ventral dissection) (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the label transfer analysis.

claim: Differentially expressed genes in A(1) were enriched for genes associated with regulation of negative chemotaxis, dorsal/ventral axon guidance, and V-SVZ-to-OB migration.
source: Differentially expressed genes in A(1) were enriched for genes associated with particular neurite outgrowth and migratory programs, such as regulation of negative chemotaxis (GO:0050923), dorsal/ventral axon guidance (GO:0033563), and V-SVZ-to-OB migration (GO:0022028), suggesting unique and salient features of the migration and guidance preferentially used by ventrally derived A cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Among the differentially expressed genes in cluster A(0), there was an overrepresentation of genes involved in presynaptic membrane assembly, postsynaptic density assembly, and synaptic vesicle clustering such as Nrxn1 and Nlgn1.
source: Among the differentially expressed genes in cluster A(0), we found an overrepresentation of genes involved in presynaptic membrane assembly (GO:0097105), postsynaptic density assembly (GO:0097107), and synaptic vesicle clustering (GO:0097091) such as Nrxn1 and Nlgn1 that were upregulated in dorsally derived A cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: A different set of genes involved in axon guidance was upregulated in cluster A(0), including DCC, Efna5, and Sema6d.
source: Interestingly, a different set of genes involved in axon guidance (GO:0007411) was upregulated in cluster A(0), including DCC, Efna5, and Sema6d. (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: A cells are a molecularly heterogeneous population and that heterogeneity is indicative of an A cell's region of origin within the V-SVZ.
source: Together these data suggest that A cells are a molecularly heterogeneous population and that heterogeneity is indicative of an A cell's region of origin within the V-SVZ.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of A cell heterogeneity.

claim: Four genes were expressed throughout the dorsal lineage (Rlbp1, Gm29260, Pax6, and Dcc).
source: We identified four genes that were expressed throughout the dorsal lineage (Rlbp1, Gm29260, Pax6, and Dcc) and five genes expressed through the ventral lineage (Adgrl3, Slit2, Ptprn2, Rbms1, Sntb1) (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a finding from the lineage marker analysis.

claim: Five genes were expressed through the ventral lineage (Adgrl3, Slit2, Ptprn2, Rbms1, Sntb1).
source: We identified four genes that were expressed throughout the dorsal lineage (Rlbp1, Gm29260, Pax6, and Dcc) and five genes expressed through the ventral lineage (Adgrl3, Slit2, Ptprn2, Rbms1, Sntb1) (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a finding from the lineage marker analysis.

claim: B(14) and A(1), and B(5+22) and A(0) had a higher degree of transcriptional overlap, and correspond to ventral and dorsal lineages, respectively.
source: This suggests that B(14) and A(1), and B(5+22) and A(0) had a higher degree of transcriptional overlap, and correspond to ventral and dorsal lineages, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lineage marker analysis.

claim: The scores of the combined expression for dorsal and ventral lineage signatures were relatively constant throughout the B-C-A cell lineage progression.
source: However, the scores of the combined expression for dorsal and ventral lineage signatures were relatively constant throughout the B-C-A cell lineage progression (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a finding from the AUC score analysis.

claim: 257 significantly differentially expressed genes were identified between the High Score lineages: 108 dorsal markers and 149 ventral markers.
source: We identified 257 significantly differentially expressed genes between the High Score lineages: 108 dorsal markers and 149 ventral markers (Figure 6H; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Among the differentially expressed genes in the High Score dorsal B cells, there was an overrepresentation of the thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion with higher expression of Dio2 and Slc16a2.
source: Among the differentially expressed genes in the High Score dorsal B cells, we found an overrepresentation of the thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion (GO:0070460) with higher expression of Dio2 and Slc16a2.
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Hes1 and Hes5, commonly used as readouts of Notch activation, were upregulated in the High Score dorsal B cells.
source: Hes1 and Hes5, commonly used as readouts of Notch activation (Ohtsuka et al., 1999), were upregulated in the High Score dorsal B cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis, with a supporting citation.

claim: The High Score ventral B cells had an enrichment in genes involved in dorsal/ventral pattern formation, response to laminar fluid shear stress, adherens junction assembly, and cerebrospinal fluid circulation.
source: The High Score ventral B cells had an enrichment in genes involved in dorsal/ventral pattern formation (GO:0009953), response to laminar fluid shear stress (GO:0034616), adherens junction assembly (GO:0034333), and cerebrospinal fluid circulation (GO:0090660).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Dorsal A cells had a higher expression of Nlgn1 and Nrxn1, genes in the NMDA glutamate receptor clustering category.
source: Dorsal A cells had a higher expression of Nlgn1 and Nrxn1, genes in the NMDA glutamate receptor clustering category, and also had presynaptic membrane assembly (GO:0097105) and semaphorin-plexin signaling (GO:0071526) categories overrepresented.
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: High Score ventral A cells were strongly enriched in Slit1, Slit2, and Robo1, genes involved in the regulation of negative chemotaxis.
source: High Score ventral A cells were strongly enriched in Slit1, Slit2, and Robo1, genes involved in the regulation of negative chemotaxis (GO:0050923).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: The putative dorsal lineage genes Pax6 and Rlbp1 were highly enriched in the dorsal region of the V-SVZ, with particularly enriched expression in the 'wedge' region.
source: We found that the putative dorsal lineage genes Pax6 and Rlbp1 were highly enriched in the dorsal region of the V-SVZ, with particularly enriched expression in the 'wedge' region (Figure 6I–L,O; Figure 6—figure supplement 1I–L).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAscope validation experiments.

claim: The putative ventral markers Adgrl3 and Slit2 had a higher expression in the ventral domain of the V-SVZ.
source: Conversely, the putative ventral markers Adgrl3 and Slit2 had a higher expression in the ventral domain of the V-SVZ (Figure 6P–S,V; Figure 6—figure supplement 1L–O).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAscope validation experiments.

claim: Regional allocations of the neuroepithelium during brain development give NSPCs different neurogenic properties.
source: During brain development, regional allocations of the neuroepithelium give NSPCs different neurogenic properties.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in developmental neuroscience.

claim: The adult V-SVZ neurogenic niche retains regionally specified NSPCs that generate different subtypes of neurons destined for the OB.
source: The adult V-SVZ neurogenic niche retains regionally specified NSPCs that generate different subtypes of neurons destined for the OB.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge and the findings of this study.

claim: The scRNA-Seq and sNucRNA-Seq datasets provide new information about the diverse cell types that populate the V-SVZ.
source: Our scRNA-Seq and sNucRNA-Seq datasets provide new information about the diverse cell types that populate the V-SVZ.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the study.

claim: Lineage analysis reveals parallel pathways of neurogenesis initiated by different populations of B cells.
source: Our lineage analysis reveals parallel pathways of neurogenesis initiated by different populations of B cells.
evidence: This is a summary of a key finding from the lineage analysis.

claim: Regional differences in NSPCs potential were demonstrated using restricted viral labeling of non-overlapping territories of the V-SVZ.
source: Regional differences in NSPCs potential were demonstrated using restricted viral labeling of non-overlapping territories of the V-SVZ (Merkle et al., 2014; Merkle et al., 2007; Ventura and Goldman, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous viral labeling studies.

claim: Labeled ventral B cells produced deep layer granule neurons, calbindin-positive periglomerular cells, and type 1–4 cells in the OB.
source: Labeled ventral B cells produced deep layer granule neurons, calbindin-positive periglomerular cells, and type 1–4 cells in the OB, while dorsal B cells produced superficial granule neurons and tyrosine hydroxylase-positive periglomerular cells (Merkle et al., 2014; Merkle et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous viral labeling studies.

claim: Dorsal B cells produced superficial granule neurons and tyrosine hydroxylase-positive periglomerular cells.
source: Labeled ventral B cells produced deep layer granule neurons, calbindin-positive periglomerular cells, and type 1–4 cells in the OB, while dorsal B cells produced superficial granule neurons and tyrosine hydroxylase-positive periglomerular cells (Merkle et al., 2014; Merkle et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous viral labeling studies.

claim: Genetic lineage tracing from territories expressing regionally restricted transcription factors indicates that NSPCs in dorsal and ventral territories generate superficial and deep-layer neurons for the OB, respectively.
source: Similarly, genetic lineage tracing from territories expressing regionally restricted transcription factors also indicates that NSPCs in dorsal and ventral territories generate superficial and deep-layer neurons for the OB, respectively (Kohwi et al., 2007; Kohwi et al., 2005; Merkle et al., 2014; Young et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous genetic lineage tracing studies.

claim: Regionally specified NSPCs can be lineage traced to the embryo.
source: However, regionally specified NSPCs can be lineage traced to the embryo (Fuentealba et al., 2015; Furutachi et al., 2015), and we could not detect a population of Oct4+ cells in our datasets.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous lineage tracing studies.

claim: Genetic labeling of the most ventral domain of the V-SVZ showed the specific contribution of Nkx2.1-expressing B cells to deep layer granule cell neurons in the OB.
source: More recently, genetic labeling of the most ventral domain of the V-SVZ showed the specific contribution of Nkx2.1-expressing B cells to deep layer granule cell neurons in the OB (Delgado and Lim, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous genetic labeling study.

claim: The ventral gene expression program is maintained by an epigenetic mechanism across cell divisions.
source: The ventral gene expression program is maintained by an epigenetic mechanism across cell divisions.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: In the absence of myeloid/lymphoid or mixed-lineage leukemia protein 1 (MLL1)-dependent epigenetic maintenance, the neurogenic lineage shifts to produce aberrantly 'dorsalized' OB neuronal subtypes.
source: In the absence of myeloid/lymphoid or mixed-lineage leukemia protein 1 (MLL1)-dependent epigenetic maintenance, the neurogenic lineage shifts to produce aberrantly 'dorsalized' OB neuronal subtypes (Delgado et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The dataset is restricted to the V-SVZ, a region where A cells (young neurons) have begun their differentiation, but remain migratory and immature.
source: Our dataset is restricted to the V-SVZ, a region where A cells (young neurons) have begun their differentiation, but remain migratory and immature.
evidence: This describes the scope and limitations of the dataset.

claim: Pax6 expression is largely restricted in the dorsal lineage of A cells.
source: Consistent with these findings, we found Pax6 expression largely restricted in the dorsal lineage of A cells (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis.

claim: The new set of genes associated with young A neurons derived from dorsal or ventral territories should help future studies determine the early programs in the differentiation of specific subtypes of OB neurons.
source: The new set of genes associated with young A neurons derived from dorsal or ventral territories should help future studies determine the early programs in the differentiation of specific subtypes of OB neurons.
evidence: This is a speculation about the potential impact of the findings.

claim: The dataset provides sets of genes that are differentially expressed in dorsal and ventral B cells.
source: Our dataset provides sets of genes that are differentially expressed in dorsal and ventral B cells.
evidence: This is a summary of a key finding from the study.

claim: Urah, Dio2, and Crym were identified as novel markers that define largely non-overlapping domains of the V-SVZ.
source: We also identified Urah, Dio2, and Crym as novel markers that define largely non-overlapping domains of the V-SVZ.
evidence: This is a summary of a key finding from the study.

claim: Urah and Dio2 define a dorsal domain that includes the wedge and subcallosal roof of the V-SVZ.
source: Urah and Dio2 define a dorsal domain that includes the wedge and subcallosal roof of the V-SVZ, and Crym defines a wide ventral domain.
evidence: This is a summary of a key finding from the study.

claim: Crym defines a wide ventral domain.
source: Urah and Dio2 define a dorsal domain that includes the wedge and subcallosal roof of the V-SVZ, and Crym defines a wide ventral domain.
evidence: This is a summary of a key finding from the study.

claim: The dorsal domain overlaps with that defined by Pax6.
source: Consistent with the above observations, Crym expression has been described in a subpopulation of qNSC in the early postnatal V-SVZ derived from the Nkx2.1 domain (Borrett et al., 2020). Our dorsal domain overlaps with that defined by Pax6 (Hack et al., 2005; Kohwi et al., 2005) and the ventral domain with that defined by Vax1 (Coré et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a comparison of the findings with previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The ventral domain overlaps with that defined by Vax1.
source: Consistent with the above observations, Crym expression has been described in a subpopulation of qNSC in the early postnatal V-SVZ derived from the Nkx2.1 domain (Borrett et al., 2020). Our dorsal domain overlaps with that defined by Pax6 (Hack et al., 2005; Kohwi et al., 2005) and the ventral domain with that defined by Vax1 (Coré et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a comparison of the findings with previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Gsx2 is expressed in a gradient in the embryo, with its highest expression in the dorsal lateral ganglionic eminence.
source: Similarly, Gsx2 is expressed in a gradient in the embryo, with its highest expression in the dorsal lateral ganglionic eminence (Corbin et al., 2000; López-Juárez et al., 2013; Taglialatela et al., 2004; Waclaw et al., 2009; Young et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The dorsal region was enriched in Ptprz1, Hopx, Dio2, Tnc, and Moxd1, which are also markers of outer radial glia.
source: The dorsal region was also enriched in Ptprz1, Hopx, Dio2, Tnc, and Moxd1, which are also markers of outer radial glia, a subpopulation of human neural stem cells that continue to generate neurons for the cortex after detaching from the pallial wall of the lateral ventricles during prenatal development (Nowakowski et al., 2016; Pollen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene expression analysis, with supporting citations.

claim: The dorsal V-SVZ domain is likely further subdivided into multiple subdomains.
source: The dorsal V-SVZ domain is likely further subdivided into multiple subdomains.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the gene expression patterns.

claim: The largely pallial marker Emx1 and dorsal lateral ganglionic eminence marker Gsx2 were differentially enriched in clusters B(22) and B(5), respectively, suggesting that these two clusters may also represent different sets of regionally specified B cells with distinct embryonic origins.
source: However, the largely pallial marker Emx1 and dorsal lateral ganglionic eminence marker Gsx2 were differentially enriched in clusters B(22) and B(5), respectively, suggesting that these two clusters may also represent different sets of regionally specified B cells with distinct embryonic origins.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the differential gene expression patterns.

claim: The wedge region likely includes what has been termed the ventral pallium, which is characterized in the embryo by the expression of Dbx1.
source: In addition to pallial and dorsal subpallial markers, this wedge region likely also includes what has been termed the ventral pallium (Puelles et al., 2016), which is characterized in the embryo by the expression of Dbx1.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the location and markers, with a supporting citation.

claim: 59 genes in the scRNA-Seq analysis were highly expressed in sNucRNA-Seq B cells from the dorsal microdissection, including Pax6.
source: We also found that 59 genes in our scRNA-Seq analysis were highly expressed in sNucRNA-Seq B cells from the dorsal microdissection, including Pax6.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison of the two datasets.

claim: Seven genes were highly expressed in the ventral microdissected sNucRNA-Seq B cells that were also highly expressed in the ventral scRNA-Seq B(14) cluster, including Slit2.
source: Similarly, seven genes were highly expressed in the ventral microdissected sNucRNA-Seq B cells that were also highly expressed in the ventral scRNA-Seq B(14) cluster, including Slit2 (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison of the two datasets.

claim: The border between the Crym+ and the Urah/Dio2+ territories had not been previously determined and lies in an anatomically undefined location.
source: The border between the Crym+ and the Urah/Dio2+ territories had not been previously determined and lies in an anatomically undefined location (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the validation experiments.

claim: The dorsal domain defined by Dio2 and Urah largely overlaps with a region of high Gli1 expression during neonatal and early postnatal stages.
source: Interestingly, the dorsal domain defined by Dio2 and Urah largely overlaps with a region of high Gli1 expression during neonatal and early postnatal stages (Tong et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison of the findings with a previous study, supported by a citation.

claim: This dorsal Sonic Hedgehog-regulated domain in early postnatal life has been linked to oligodendrogenesis.
source: This dorsal Sonic Hedgehog-regulated domain in early postnatal life has been linked to oligodendrogenesis.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Thyroid hormone signaling has been shown to regulate V-SVZ neurogenesis.
source: Thyroid hormone signaling has been shown to regulate V-SVZ neurogenesis (Lemkine et al., 2005; López-Juárez et al., 2012; Luongo et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are all associated with the thyroid hormone signaling pathway.
source: Our analysis shows that Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are differentially expressed by B cells according to region. Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are all associated with the thyroid hormone signaling pathway; Dio2 catalyzes thyroid hormone activation, Crym has been described to bind thyroid hormone, and Urah belongs to a family of thyroid hormone transporters (Luongo et al., 2019; Rudqvist et al., 2012; Vié et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Dio2 catalyzes thyroid hormone activation.
source: Our analysis shows that Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are differentially expressed by B cells according to region. Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are all associated with the thyroid hormone signaling pathway; Dio2 catalyzes thyroid hormone activation, Crym has been described to bind thyroid hormone, and Urah belongs to a family of thyroid hormone transporters (Luongo et al., 2019; Rudqvist et al., 2012; Vié et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Crym has been described to bind thyroid hormone.
source: Our analysis shows that Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are differentially expressed by B cells according to region. Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are all associated with the thyroid hormone signaling pathway; Dio2 catalyzes thyroid hormone activation, Crym has been described to bind thyroid hormone, and Urah belongs to a family of thyroid hormone transporters (Luongo et al., 2019; Rudqvist et al., 2012; Vié et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Urah belongs to a family of thyroid hormone transporters.
source: Our analysis shows that Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are differentially expressed by B cells according to region. Crym, Urah, and Dio2 are all associated with the thyroid hormone signaling pathway; Dio2 catalyzes thyroid hormone activation, Crym has been described to bind thyroid hormone, and Urah belongs to a family of thyroid hormone transporters (Luongo et al., 2019; Rudqvist et al., 2012; Vié et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Hormone signaling, and in particular thyroid hormones, may differentially affect B cells in a regional manner and possibly modify the balance of neuronal types produced in the V-SVZ and destined for the OB.
source: Hormone signaling, and in particular thyroid hormones, may differentially affect B cells in a regional manner and possibly modify the balance of neuronal types produced in the V-SVZ and destined for the OB.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings.

claim: Region-specific regulation of V-SVZ stem cells has been previously suggested for the anterior-ventral V-SVZ, where a subpopulation of proopiomelanocortin hypothalamic projections activates Nkx2.1+ progenitors.
source: Region-specific regulation of V-SVZ stem cells has been previously suggested for the anterior-ventral V-SVZ, where a subpopulation of proopiomelanocortin hypothalamic projections activates Nkx2.1+ progenitors (Paul et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The combination of region-specific innervation and molecular composition of B cells could form the basis for a system of hormonal regulation underlying circuit changes in the OB.
source: The combination of region-specific innervation and molecular composition of B cells could form the basis for a system of hormonal regulation underlying circuit changes in the OB.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings and previous knowledge.

claim: The study presents a large-scale single-cell description of dorso-ventral identity in the lateral wall of the V-SVZ.
source: In summary, we present a large-scale single-cell description of dorso-ventral identity in the lateral wall of the V-SVZ.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the study.

claim: The study recapitulates known divisions between dorsal and ventral B cells.
source: Not only do we recapitulate known divisions between dorsal and ventral B cells, but also we identify novel regional B cell markers and uncover gene expression programs that appear to persist throughout lineage transitions (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the study.

claim: The study identifies novel regional B cell markers.
source: Not only do we recapitulate known divisions between dorsal and ventral B cells, but also we identify novel regional B cell markers and uncover gene expression programs that appear to persist throughout lineage transitions (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the study.

claim: The study uncovers gene expression programs that appear to persist throughout lineage transitions.
source: Not only do we recapitulate known divisions between dorsal and ventral B cells, but also we identify novel regional B cell markers and uncover gene expression programs that appear to persist throughout lineage transitions (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the study.

claim: The data form a basis for future investigation of NSPCs identity, lineage commitment, and embryonic origin.
source: These data form a basis for future investigation of NSPCs identity, lineage commitment, and embryonic origin, providing clues to help us understand how molecularly defined stem cell territories are spatially organized, and what distinguishes V-SVZ regions from one another.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential impact of the findings.
